title: Fewest Arrows to Turn to Reach the Corner

concept.title: Free moves and cost-1 moves: a deque instead of a priority queue (0-1 BFS)
body: Every cell of a grid holds an arrow: `R`, `L`, `D` or `U`. Standing on a cell, you may follow its arrow to the next cell **for free**. You may also step to any other neighbouring cell, but then you have to **turn the arrow** of the cell you leave, which costs **1**. What is the smallest total cost to get from the top left cell to the bottom right cell? Each arrow can be turned at most once in any useful path, so the cost is simply the number of steps that do not follow the arrow.

This is a shortest path problem where every edge costs **0** or **1**. Dijkstra's algorithm works, but there is a simpler tool, *0-1 BFS*: keep a **deque** of cells. When the move costs 0, push the new cell to the **front**; when it costs 1, push it to the **back**. The deque then always stays sorted by distance (the front has the smallest distance, and the back has at most one more), so cells come out in the order of increasing distance without a heap, in O(1) per push.

A cell may be pushed more than once (when a shorter distance is found later), so the check `dist + cost < dist[a][b]` is needed; a cell is only expanded with its best distance because older, larger entries find nothing to improve. The time is O(h * w) with four moves per cell. Whenever the edge costs take only two values that differ by one, think of a deque.

statement: A grid has `h` rows and `w` columns; every cell holds an arrow `R` (right), `L` (left), `D` (down) or `U` (up). From a cell you can move to one of its four neighbours (inside the grid). The move along the arrow of the cell costs 0; a move in any other direction costs 1 (the arrow of the cell is turned). Print the smallest total cost of a path from the top left cell to the bottom right cell.
inputFormat: The first line has `h` and `w`: the number of rows and columns.
Each of the next `h` lines has a row of `w` characters: `R`, `L`, `D` or `U`.

examples.note: Follow the arrows right, right, down to the bottom right cell: cost 0.
Both moves (right and down) have to be bought: cost 2.

hints: Think of the cells as nodes; a move along the arrow costs 0 and any other move costs 1.
Use a deque: a cost-0 move goes to the front, a cost-1 move goes to the back.
Update a cell only when you find a strictly smaller distance.

explanation: 0-1 BFS: a deque holds the cells; moving along the arrow costs 0 and puts the cell at the front, any other move costs 1 and puts it at the back. A cell is pushed again only when a strictly smaller distance is found, and the distance of the last cell is printed.
solution.complexity: Time O(h * w), space O(h * w).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

h, w = map(int, input().split())
grid = [input().strip() for _ in range(h)]

from collections import deque
INF = 10 ** 9
letters = "RLDU"
moves = ((0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0))
dist = [[INF] * w for _ in range(h)]
dist[0][0] = 0
queue = deque([(0, 0)])
while queue:
    x, y = queue.popleft()
    for d in range(4):
        a, b = x + moves[d][0], y + moves[d][1]
        if 0 <= a < h and 0 <= b < w:
            cost = 0 if grid[x][y] == letters[d] else 1
            if dist[x][y] + cost < dist[a][b]:
                dist[a][b] = dist[x][y] + cost
                if cost == 0:
                    queue.appendleft((a, b))
                else:
                    queue.append((a, b))
print(dist[h - 1][w - 1])
